message: Relation field "Post.author": @relation argument "onDelete" is not supported; Prisma 8 enforces no referential actions on MongoDB. The Prisma 6 client emulates referential actions, so removing "onDelete: Cascade" also changes the Prisma 6 app: its client then applies Restrict, its default for a required relation, so deleting a User that still has Post documents fails with P2014. Handle related documents in application code, then remove "onDelete".

Relation field "Post.author": @relation argument "onUpdate" is not supported; Prisma 8 enforces no referential actions on MongoDB. The Prisma 6 client emulates referential actions, so removing "onUpdate: Restrict" also changes the Prisma 6 app: its client then applies Cascade, its default, so changing the field a Post refers to in a User updates the key in its Post documents. Handle related documents in application code, then remove "onUpdate".

Relation field "Comment.author": @relation argument "onUpdate" is not supported; Prisma 8 enforces no referential actions on MongoDB. Removing "onUpdate: Cascade" leaves the Prisma 6 app as it is: Cascade is already what the Prisma 6 client does for this relation. Handle related documents in application code, then remove "onUpdate".

Relation field "Comment.author": @relation argument "onDelete" is not supported; Prisma 8 enforces no referential actions on MongoDB. Removing "onDelete: SetNull" leaves the Prisma 6 app as it is: SetNull is already what the Prisma 6 client does for this relation. Handle related documents in application code, then remove "onDelete".

Relation field "Like.user": @relation argument "map" is not supported; it names a foreign key constraint, and MongoDB has none. Remove "map"; the Prisma 6 app has no foreign key on MongoDB either, so nothing changes there.

Relation field "Reaction.user": @relation argument "onDelete" is not supported; Prisma 8 enforces no referential actions on MongoDB. The Prisma 6 client emulates referential actions, so removing "onDelete: Cascade" also changes the Prisma 6 app: its client then applies SetNull, its default for an optional relation, so deleting a User sets the key to null in its Reaction documents. Handle related documents in application code, then remove "onDelete".
